annotations.text:
Direction E — the whole app.

Seven screens plus the baseline, all in one language: cool neutrals, 6px radii, 28px controls, indigo accent, real elevation, system-ui throughout.

The structural move is that work is first-class and stage is a property. Today everything is stage-first — pick a stage, then see its risks. Here the sidebar's views cut across all 23 stages, and a stage is a filter, a group header and a page of its own. Two of the four ways of opening things are gone: the Main/Dashboard toggle (Dashboard is now the Overview view) and the 1120px modal (now a peek panel or a page).

Real AtlasAX1 seed, 23-stage built-in profile, 1440px.

OVERVIEW — the old Dashboard, no longer a mode you toggle into. Five stat cards, then the schedule kept deliberately first-class on the left (answering the fair objection that E demotes the timeline), the update feed under it, and in-flight stages plus checkpoints on the right.

TIMELINE — a full view rather than a 240px strip. 26px rows grouped by lifecycle phase, so 23 stages are readable and a phase carries its own risk count. Bars are draggable: the selected one shows its handles and the tooltip states the ripple rule out loud. Zoom is week / month / quarter.

STAGE › ACTIVITY — the two lists have merged into one tab.

The template's 11 engineering activities for TEST, in work order, each showing STEPS as a segmented bar plus "n of m". Under them, a divider, then the free-form items added on this program. One list, two kinds, told apart by the ref chip and the step bar.

Real data: TEST has 11 activities and 86 steps; 21 are done today. The deliverable rail now says which step ticks each deliverable — producedBy already names it on all 257 activities.

STAGE › ACTIVITY, EXPANDED — TEST-03 opened in place. Its 8 authored steps become a checklist: parallel steps are marked and indented, each step shows what it adds, its window, and how many posts mention it. Step 8 carries "TICKS TEST-D2" — completing that step is what completes the deliverable.

The panel holds ONE thread for the activity, and each post carries an optional step tag. Look at the top post: it is tagged STEP 6, which has not started yet. That is the point of tagging rather than nesting — you flag a problem on the step it will hit, months before you get there.

RISKS — the cross-stage work view, and where a TPM starts the day. Grouped by stage rather than contained by it; the aggregate boards (Open Risks, Overdue, Status Updates) stop being a special modal and become saved views. Same peek panel as Stage › Activity, one level up.

PROGRAMS — today this page is one card in a mostly empty 1440px screen. Here it is a table that reads the same at one program and at twenty, with a preview panel so you can judge a program before entering it. Only AtlasAX1 exists in the seed, so only AtlasAX1 is shown — the empty state below the row is deliberate, not a placeholder.

ACTIVITY DETAIL — where "Read TEST-03 →" lands, and where a row in the Activity tab lands. A page, not a panel: it is long, it is linked, and it is the same on every program running this template.

"How it gets there" is the same 8 steps you tick in the stage — here they are read with their full text and lane diagram, there they are worked.

Open question: today this page is Georgia and it is the best-reading screen in the app. E has no serif, so this is system-ui 15px / 1.65. Keeping the serif would make it the one deliberate exception.

DESIGN SYSTEM — every value used on the seven screens, with the old-token-to-new mapping. This is the sheet the next step turns into globals.css. Note what gets deleted: --serif, --mono, --title-size, and one of the two caption systems.
TODAY — the baseline, for comparison. Top 1560px only; the scroll continues past it.

Explorations, kept for reference. A/B/C were round one — three structures in the app's existing skin, which is why none of them answered "it looks dated". D and F were round two alongside E. The token audit at the end still measures the app as it stands today.

ACTIVITY & STEP MODEL — what changes in the schema, and the numbers that argue for it. Two new tables, both lazy, plus one optional field on StatusUpdate. The free-form Item stays, because work outside the template still has to be recorded somewhere.
